maria: Ran an nsys capture on the 8xA100 inference job (batching=dynamic, kv-cache enabled). Seeing large idle gaps on ranks 2-5 between forward kernels.

jon: Can you paste the command you used and the brief timeline screenshot?

maria: Command: ```nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl --output=run_8xA100 -t 30 -- ./bin/serve --model resnetlike --gpus 8 --batching auto```

maria: Perfetto link (full trace): https://perfetto.dev/trace/zzR7aQ (timeline shows repeated pattern: compute -> NCCL allreduce -> 30-50ms gap -> next compute)

alex: Interesting — gap coincides with KV cache handshake in logs? Any kv-cache retire spikes?

maria: Logs show kv-cache retire/restore messages on ranks 1/3/4 right before the gaps. snippet: ```[KV] retire range 0x7f8.. len=512k; restoring KV segment took 27ms```.

jon: That matches. My hypothesis: our kernel selector is choosing a slower kernel variant when sequence-length distribution changes after restore, causing additional compilation or warmup cost. Could also be NCCL re-sync due to buffer registration reorder.

sandhya: On the trace, NCCL allreduce overlaps partially with compute on rank0 but fully serializes on ranks 2-5. Did you capture the NVTX marks for batching boundaries?

maria: Yes NVTX marks present. Markers show batch pack/unpack around the allreduce. Continuous batching queue length spikes just before the stall.

alex: Do we see any PCIe memcpy spikes or P2P fallbacks on those ranks?

maria: Small memcpy bursts (~4ms) on ranks 2/4 after kv-restore, but nothing huge. No P2P fallback flags in nsys.

jon: Two actionable leads: (1) kernel selector path: check if we hit a fallback kernel (e.g., int8->fp16) after cache restore, and avoid re-querying kernels synchronously; (2) NCCL: enable async progress or tune op size to avoid serialization.

sandhya: Also test disabling KV retire on a subset to verify causality. If gaps disappear, we know ordering between cache ops and collective triggers the stall.

maria: Agreed. I'll run three quick experiments tomorrow: A) disable kv-retire on ranks 2-5; B) pin kernel variant by forcing kernel_id env var; C) run with NCCL_ASYNC_PROGRESS=1 and collect nsys.

jon: For (B) add `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=fast_fp16` env and run short 20s capture. Also add `--nvtx-annotations` to get clearer markers.

trace-bot: New capture queued: run_8xA100_kvtest_A (1766270001).

maria: Thanks. One more note — batching heuristic: when prefix length > 32, we fall back to a different batching strategy which may trigger different memory layout. Could be related. I'll log prefix stats.

alex: If you need a quick perf patch, I can instrument kernel-selector to early bail when a cached kernel exists for identical tensor shapes. Might reduce the sync.

maria: Please do. For now I'll collect the three traces and post flamegraphs. If disabling kv-retire removes the gap, next step is reordering retire to be async and decouple from collective epochs.

jon: Cool. Keep notes brief in this thread and drop links to captures. :thumbsup:

maria: Will do — first capture uploads in ~2h.
